Australia.details: Pedestrians are legally mandated to use a pedestrian crossing (such as zebra crossings or traffic signals) if they are within 20 meters of one. These traffic regulations apply strictly to public roads and thoroughfares; internal pedestrian movement within private shopping centers, commercial retail complexes, or university campuses is exempt from these statutory provisions.
Australia.fines: Varies by state; ranges from AUD 77 in New South Wales (NSW Roads Act 1993 s. 125) to AUD 100+ in Queensland and Victoria. Police issue immediate on-the-spot infringement notices.

Looking at the road ahead in these images, taken in the seconds before the pedestrian crosses: the pedestrian crosses at an intersection, that is a place where another public road joins or crosses this road, with the kerb corners or the side road visible on at least one side of the crossing place. Answer NO when the crossing place is on a straight stretch between junctions, or at the exit of a yard, a car park, a petrol station, or a private driveway. Answer UNKNOWN when the road cannot be seen well enough to tell.

United States.basis: Illegal in most states (State and Municipal Traffic Codes)
United States.details: Jaywalking legislation is entirely state and municipal. Recent legislative trends have seen major decriminalization: California enacted AB 2147 (Freedom to Walk Act), allowing police to cite pedestrians only when an immediate collision hazard exists, and New York City decriminalized jaywalking in 2023. Other states (e.g., Texas, Florida) retain traditional enforcement. Spatial Jurisdiction Clarification: Statutes apply strictly to public roadways and streets; crossing inside private shopping malls, corporate parks, or university campuses does not constitute statutory jaywalking.
United States.fines: Fines where enforced range from $25 to $250 USD.
United States.decision: All required conditions YES → JAYWALKING under that jurisdiction's code. Because the offense is defined stateand municipality-wide, the jurisdiction gate (condition 3) is decisive: if it cannot be resolved from location metadata it must be UNKNOWN → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

Bangladesh.basis: Illegal (Road Transport Act, 2018, section 42(3), penalty section 85). Section 42(3): "প্রত্যেক সড়ক ব্যবহারকারীকে সড়ক বা মহাসড়ক পারাপারে নির্দিষ্ট জেব্রা ক্রসিং, ফুটওভার ব্রিজ, আন্ডারপাস বা অনুরূপ সুবিধা, যদি থাকে, ব্যবহার করিতে হইবে।" (Every road user must use the designated zebra crossing, foot overbridge, underpass or similar facility, if there is one, to cross a road or highway.)
Bangladesh.source: Road Transport Act, 2018 (Act No. 47 of 2018), in force 1 November 2019. Bangla text of section 42 and 85 read at https://lawsofbangladesh.mintlify.app/laws/act-1262 (a mirror of bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd), and confirmed by press reports of the 1 month / BDT 10,000 penalty. The official text is at https://legislativediv.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/legislativediv.portal.gov.bd/page/c0e8021e_5e8f_4ede_9050_f2faf351c2ad/24.%20Road%20Transport%20Act,%202018.pdf
Bangladesh.details: The duty applies to every road user and only where a crossing facility exists ('if any'). The Act sets no distance. Foot overbridges and underpasses count as facilities, so a pedestrian who crosses the carriageway beneath or beside a footbridge commits the offence even when no zebra crossing is near.
Bangladesh.fines: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or a fine up to BDT 10,000, or both (Road Transport Act 2018, section 85, for violating section 42).
Bangladesh.decision: All required conditions YES → JAYWALKING. Any required condition NO → NOT_JAYWALKING. Any required condition UNKNOWN → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
